statusDetail: Coverage-complete agentic audit of four representative public templates plus a failure route.

page.framework: Hand-authored server-rendered HTML with inline CSS/JS behind Cloudflare
page.notes: Public URL protection/shortening and monetisation service. Homepage, authentication, contact, policy, and 404 surfaces sampled. DMCA was not separately audited because it is a low-risk legal-content template represented by policy.html.

paths.description: Homepage and advertised link-protection journey; primary product template and core task.
Login/signup destination; representative authentication and account flow.
Contact form; representative secondary form and support journey.
Privacy policy; representative long-form/legal content template.
Unknown route; representative HTTP/network recovery state.

findings.summary: The public pages ignore the user’s dark theme preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical to the default capture; the inline CSS hard-codes light surfaces and declares neither color-scheme nor a dark media query.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and supply preference-driven light/dark tokens with sufficient contrast.

findings.summary: Navigation and state changes have no transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found no view-transition rules, while login, policy, and contact are distinct same-origin documents that switch abruptly.
findings.suggestedFix: Add progressive cross-document View Transitions for same-origin navigation, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Standalone pages provide no orientation or route back to the service.
findings.evidence: Login, policy, and contact DOM snapshots contain no nav landmark or home link; the login screenshot is an isolated panel.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a consistent semantic header/nav with current-page context and a clear route home.

findings.summary: The homepage overflows horizontally on a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout primitive measured scrollWidth 390 versus clientWidth 360 (30 px overflow), and the screenshot clips the card at the right edge.
findings.suggestedFix: Use border-box sizing and intrinsic/fluid widths so padded 100% containers and controls stay within the viewport.

findings.summary: Reusable cards and controls only react to the viewport, not their available container.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no container queries; CSS uses one global max-width breakpoint while the same card/form pattern appears at multiple widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable form/card wrappers an inline-size container and adapt child spacing/type with @container where reuse requires it.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is removed from the primary inputs.
findings.evidence: The focus probe reports outline none and no box shadow for all three homepage inputs; footer links are only 16–17 px high.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a strong :focus-visible ring and increase compact link hit areas without removing native focus.

findings.summary: The advertised link-protection task cannot be completed.
findings.evidence: The homepage presents URL, title, and size inputs but the rendered DOM contains zero forms and no submit button or action; the screenshot ends the card with an empty rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the fields in a real form, provide a clearly labelled submit control, validate the URL/name format, and return a usable protected-link result.

findings.summary: Failure and recovery states are absent or non-actionable.
findings.evidence: The login flow always invokes a blocking alert saying only “This username and password not found”; the primary homepage has no submission state, and the 404 page offers no recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide inline, accessible status regions and specific retry/back/home actions for form, auth, and HTTP error states.

findings.summary: Delivery is fast but cache and dependency hygiene can improve.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports inefficient cache lifetimes (about 7 KiB potential savings); the HAR records a redirected Cloudflare script request.
findings.suggestedFix: Set useful cache lifetimes for stable assets and avoid avoidable redirect/dependency hops.

findings.summary: Third-party JavaScript dominates this tiny page and is mostly unused.
findings.evidence: The HAR attributes 166,815 of 184,990 transferred bytes to Google Tag Manager, while Lighthouse estimates 68 KiB of unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove analytics if it does not support a defined need, or load a smaller, consent-aware analytics path after interaction/idle.

findings.summary: The primary inputs have no programmatic labels and the page lacks semantic landmarks.
findings.evidence: The probe reports empty labels for the textarea and both inputs; visible text is implemented with center/b tags rather than label elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Associate each control with a real label and organize the page with header, nav, main, and footer landmarks.

findings.summary: Text contrast fails automated accessibility testing.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse scored the color-contrast audit 0; the visual captures show light secondary text and blue links on light surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust text/link color tokens to meet WCAG AA in every theme and verify with automated and visual checks.

findings.summary: Heading and focus structure is not logical.
findings.evidence: The homepage has no h1–h3 and starts all sections at h4, has no landmarks, and removes focus outlines from form controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one descriptive h1, a sequential heading hierarchy, semantic landmarks, and visible focus styles.

findings.summary: The homepage prevents user scaling and fails narrow reflow.
findings.evidence: The viewport meta sets maximum-scale=1 and user-scalable=no; Lighthouse failed meta-viewport and the mobile layout has 30 px overflow.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove scaling restrictions and fix intrinsic sizing so content reflows at zoom and narrow widths.

findings.summary: Deprecated platform usage remains on the page.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three deprecation warnings; DOM inspection also shows obsolete center and font elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace obsolete presentational markup with semantic HTML and CSS, then resolve each DevTools deprecation warning.

findings.summary: Metadata is generic or missing across representative pages.
findings.evidence: The homepage title is only “Linkmake”; login and contact DOM snapshots have no meta description, so titles/descriptions do not uniquely describe each surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Write a unique descriptive title and concise meta description for each public route.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals are missing.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no canonical link and /sitemap.xml returned 404, despite robots allowing indexing.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish canonical URLs and an XML sitemap covering the public routes, and reference it from robots.txt.

findings.summary: The public service has no social-preview or structured entity metadata.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found zero Open Graph tags and zero JSON-LD blocks on the homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Open Graph metadata and appropriate schema.org Organization/WebSite or WebApplication JSON-LD.

findings.summary: HTTPS is present, but transport/header and cookie defaults are unsafe.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no CSP, HSTS, or nosniff header; analytics cookies are not Secure and use SameSite=None for 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, a restrictive CSP, nosniff, and Secure/Lax cookies with proportionate lifetimes.

findings.summary: Analytics runs immediately without an evident consent or minimisation mechanism.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence identifies Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics; 90% of transferred bytes are third-party and two 400-day analytics cookies are set on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Justify and disclose collection, gate non-essential analytics on consent, shorten retention, and prefer minimal first-party measurement.

findings.summary: The authentication surface is a non-functional password-only dead end.
findings.evidence: Both Login and Signup links target login.html; submitting any credentials always triggers the same client-side alert, with no passkey or actual authentication path.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement real server-backed authentication, separate sign-up, correct autocomplete, and offer passkeys/WebAuthn.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence reports no clickjacking control, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP, or HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options), Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, HSTS, and a nonce/hash-based CSP.

findings.summary: HTTP failures do not preserve context or support recovery.
findings.evidence: A representative missing route returns the default nginx 404 with no site identity, search, home link, retry, or support route.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded, lightweight error document with a home link and actionable recovery guidance.

findings.summary: The English language is declared, but layout CSS is not writing-mode resilient.
findings.evidence: All sampled pages use lang=en, but the CSS probe found no logical properties and source uses physical padding-left/alignment patterns.
findings.suggestedFix: Retain correct lang and migrate layout edges to logical properties; set dir where content language requires it.

findings.summary: Commercial values and dates are hard-coded rather than locale-aware.
findings.evidence: Visible content hard-codes “$20”, “$4”, “2024”, and “2025”; no locale-aware formatting or locale selector is exposed.
findings.suggestedFix: Format currency and dates from structured values with Intl and document the supported locale strategy.

findings.summary: Navigation labels promise capabilities that are not delivered.
findings.evidence: “Signup” routes to the same login page as “Login”, and every login submission is rejected client-side regardless of credentials.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove misleading actions until they work, or implement distinct, honest signup/login flows and clear service availability.

findings.summary: Form errors are not humane or accessible.
findings.evidence: The login error is a generic blocking alert; homepage instructions warn of errors but provide no form submission or inline validation.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction, connect field errors with aria-describedby/aria-invalid, and announce a specific summary in a live region.

findings.summary: Inputs omit autocomplete assistance.
findings.evidence: The login probe reports empty autocomplete on username/password; homepage and contact inputs likewise expose no autocomplete tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Add username/current-password, name, email, url, and other appropriate autocomplete/inputmode tokens.

findings.summary: Account and earning claims lack a usable, reversible account journey.
findings.evidence: The homepage promotes earnings, referral bonuses, payout, signup, and login, but signup is not distinct and login never authenticates; no account-management or cancellation path was discoverable.
findings.suggestedFix: Only advertise operational account features, provide clear signup/login/account-management journeys, and disclose commitments and reversal paths.

findings.summary: Background analytics work is disproportionate to the page’s functionality.
findings.evidence: The page itself is a few kilobytes, but automatic analytics and challenge scripts create six additional requests and most transferred bytes without aiding the broken core task.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer or remove non-essential background work and measure only events tied to a documented product need.

findings.summary: The third-party budget is disproportionate for a static form page.
findings.evidence: The HAR reports 166,815 third-party bytes out of 184,990 total, almost entirely Google Tag Manager; there are no image or media assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party byte/request budget and replace or defer analytics until it provides clear user value.

taskList.title: Restore an end-to-end protected-link creation flow
Implement honest, functional signup/login and account journeys
Repair labels, landmarks, headings, focus, contrast, zoom and reflow
Deploy security headers and safe cookie defaults
Add humane inline validation and recovery states
Complete metadata, canonical, sitemap and share previews
